title: TN-Check: CSL Model Checking on Tensor-Train Compressed Chemical Master Equations
consensus_strengths: First implementation of CSL model-checking operators on tensor-network compressed state representations — a genuinely novel contribution bridging two mature fields.
Complexity separation theorem (Theorem 3) for modular CTMCs provides theoretical justification for TT-based verification: polynomial in module size, exponential only in coupling.
Error-contraction theorem (Theorem 1) exploiting Metzler structure of CME generators guarantees per-step truncation errors do not amplify multiplicatively.
Pre-build validation gate with explicit go/no-go criteria (>60% of 10+ BioModels achieve χ ≤ 200) demonstrates mature scientific methodology.
Three-valued interval-arithmetic semantics for nested CSL operators is a sound and conservative approach that avoids false positives.
consensus_weaknesses: TT-SVD truncation producing negative probability entries is a critical soundness concern; clamping-error bound must be resolved before error certificates can be trusted.
TT compressibility of biological CME distributions is an empirical hypothesis without theoretical justification for the systems of interest.
Unbounded-until fixpoint iteration may fail to converge for slowly-mixing CTMCs with metastability, falling back to bounded-until with changed semantics.
Limitation to axis-aligned propositions (single-species predicates) excludes important biological properties like stoichiometric constraints.
Computational cost estimates may undercount CSL model-checking overhead on top of time integration.
actionable_recommendations: Prioritize resolving the non-negativity/clamping gap in Theorem 1 — either bound ‖p_clamped − p_SVD‖₁ tightly or implement non-negativity-preserving TT rounding.
Execute the pre-build validation gate on adversarial models (bistable switches, oscillators) before any implementation.
Investigate non-axis-aligned proposition handling via higher-rank TT masks, even at increased computational cost.
Report indeterminate fraction as a quality metric for three-valued nested CSL model checking.
